page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 32 virtual CPUs (16 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and a substantial memory allocation of 1024.0 GB RAM, yielding 32.0 GB of memory per core. Additionally, it is equipped with 7559 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, as evidenced by top-tier Geekbench multi-core scores and strong PassMark CPU scores. Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores in the top 25% and cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 3410.51 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and small-model LLM text generation, though text generation for large 70B models falls into the bottom 10% due to the lack of GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E128-32ads_v7 offers high resource density, combining a massive memory footprint with substantial local storage on a 32-vCPU profile. This makes it highly qualitative for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of paying for excess CPU cores. The server is ideally suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics, software compilation pipelines, and memory-heavy enterprise applications that require high local storage capacity and fast single-core execution.
